parsed.explanation: A national law expressly criminalises cross-dressing under the religious penal code, and morality provisions including cross-dressing are documented as enforced (a 2014 conviction; 2017 'no known convictions' is a null result, not safety). A trans visitor cannot align documents with presentation, so being outed is structurally likely at any document check. Consequences if outed: arrest, fine, short imprisonment under the presentation offence, and exposure to a regime with de jure stoning/whipping for same-sex conduct — dormant only under a moratorium revocable at will by an absolute monarch. There is no documented pattern of visitor targeting, raids, or custody abuse, and no evidence executions will resume; enforcement appears sporadic rather than a campaign. That places this above 0.25 profiles with organised raids and extortion, but well below 0.35 profiles with no criminal statute: an enforced trans-specific offence, no document recognition, extreme latent penalties, and a revocable moratorium. Thin data on border and custody treatment resolves toward the structural risk the criminalisation implies.
